title: "Getting started"
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

```{r setup}
library(sasonr)
```

## Run a SAS program

`sas_run()` takes SAS source code, runs it on the R engine and returns the
log, the listing and the WORK data sets.

```{r}
code <- "
data dm;
  input usubjid $ age sex $;
  datalines;
S01 45 M
S02 70 F
S03 .  F
;
run;

data adsl;
  set dm;
  length agegr1 $5;
  if missing(age) then agegr1 = 'Miss';
  else if age < 65 then agegr1 = '<65';
  else agegr1 = '>=65';
  put usubjid= age= agegr1=;
run;
"
res <- sas_run(code)
sas_log(res)
res$work$adsl
```

Missing values have SAS semantics (a missing numeric value is smaller than
any number), and character variables have a fixed length, here set by the
`LENGTH` statement.

## See the generated R code

`sas_translate()` shows the R code that sasonr generates for each step. Simple
steps become vectorised `dplyr` pipelines; steps with cross-row state such as
`RETAIN`, `LAG` or `FIRST.`/`LAST.` use grouped vectorised code when the
result can be proven identical, and an explicit row loop otherwise.

```{r}
code2 <- "
data lab;
  input usubjid $ visit aval;
  datalines;
S01 1 10
S01 2 12
S02 1 20
S02 2 18
;
run;

data chg;
  set lab;
  by usubjid;
  retain base;
  if first.usubjid then base = aval;
  chg = aval - base;
run;
"
tr <- sas_translate(code2)
cat(tr$steps[[2]]$code)
sas_run(code2)$work$chg
```

## Using the translation as an R script

`sas_script()` turns a translation (or the result of `sas_run()`, the trace
of that run) into a script that runs after `library(sasonr)`. Each SAS step
becomes one call of a step verb on a session: `sas_data_step()` holds the
generated code of a DATA step, PROC SORT and PROC MEANS show the options the
program gave, other steps keep their SAS text. The script gives the same WORK
data sets and the same log as `sas_run()`.

```{r}
code3 <- "
data adsl;
  input usubjid $ age;
  datalines;
S01 70
S02 41
;
run;
proc sort data=adsl out=bysubj; by descending age; run;
"
sas_script(sas_translate(code3))
```

With `tidy = TRUE`, vectorised DATA steps read and write R
variables in dplyr pipes (the script loads dplyr and tidylog); steps that need
a session run in a short session block.

```{r}
sas_script(sas_translate(code3), tidy = TRUE)
```

## Macro language

Macro processing and step execution interleave: a step is run as soon as it
is complete, so values created with `CALL SYMPUTX` are
available to the macro code that follows.

```{r}
code3 <- "
%macro check(ds);
  data _null_;
    call symputx('n', 3);
  run;
  %if &n > 2 %then %put NOTE: &ds is large;
  %else %put NOTE: &ds is small;
%mend check;
%check(adsl)
"
sas_log(sas_run(code3), echo = FALSE)
```

`echo = FALSE` leaves the program lines out: the log shows only the
messages and the PUT output.

## Unsupported features fail loudly

sasonr never guesses. A feature it does not support stops the program with
a classed condition that carries the SAS line number.

```{r, error = TRUE}
sas_run("data a; x = 1; run; proc report data=a; run;")
```

The same applies by default (`sasonr.strict = TRUE`) to functions, formats
and informats whose status in the feature registry is `approximate`
(the last bits of numeric results may not be exact, for example in the
probability functions) or `unsupported`: they stop with a `sasonr_strict_error`
condition (see `?sasonr_strict`).

```{r, error = TRUE}
sas_run("data a; p = probnorm(1.96); run;")
```

To run them anyway, with a warning of class `sasonr_strict_warning`, turn
strict mode off:

```{r}
old <- options(sasonr.strict = FALSE)
res <- suppressWarnings(sas_run("data a; p = probnorm(1.96); run;"))
res$work$a$p
options(old)
```
